description: Valid and invalid 2.2 sources outside the gate-1 corpus at every position a duration can appear in 2.2 (WP4): wait, receive or after, state after timers, on every and deadline with every unit, spaced units, leading zeros and comments inside a duration, QoS settings requestTimeout, maxLatency and maxAge with every unit next to capacity and the enum settings, policies specializing the library policy and connection redefinitions, invalid settings (capacity = 5ms, timeouts without a duration, other settings as durations, zero and unrepresentable values), zero and unrepresentable durations in every position, duplicate and replaced every entries written in different units, deadlines above periods, durations in case scripts, stale reads across literal waits, and names that look like units (ns, us, ms, s) as attributes, locals, parameters, members, operations, states and enum literals, beside durations. In 2.3 a duration literal is an expression value and PolicySetting has one form (WP4-G01, WP4-G02). Each parses with the kept 2.2 grammar. Their diagnostics (with related information), normalized ASTs and runs are recorded once from implementation 3.1.0 in recorded-wp4.json and compared by scripts/compatibility-2-2-extended.mjs.

models.name: d1 wait with every unit, spaced units and unit names as locals (runs)
d2 receive or after with every unit and a timeout taken (runs)
d3 state timers with every unit, equal expiry in declaration order, states named like units (runs)
d4 periods and deadlines with every unit and spaced units (runs)
d5 duplicate every entries with equal nanoseconds in different units
d6 inheritance replaces an every entry written in another unit (runs)
d7 QoS duration settings with every unit, capacity beside them, connected request timeout (runs)
d8 request timeout from a policy (runs the timing out system)
d9 invalid duration settings: capacity as a duration, timeouts without durations, other settings as durations
d10 duration ranges: zero and unrepresentable waits, timeouts, timers, periods and deadlines
d11 unit names as attributes, parameters, members, operations and enum literals (runs)
d12 a name like a unit next to a duration, in a while limit and a wait
d13 durations in case scripts: waits and receive timeouts with every unit (cases)
d14 deadline above period, deadline violation and a concurrent periodic entry (runs)
d14b a deadline violation from a spaced literal deadline (runs)
d15 stale reads across literal waits and receive timeouts (warnings)
d16 a duration where an int is expected and an int where a duration is expected (parse-valid forms only)
d17 policies from the library, a policy specializing a library policy, an inline literal policy reference (runs)
d18 after chains next to state after timers and periodic deadlines (runs)
d19 durations with leading zeros and a comment between value and unit
d20 a redefined component and redefined attribute next to literal periods (runs)
d21 deadlines on receive and call entries, waits inside an interruptible region (runs)
